duplicate_row_semantics: A duplicate ROW is a second serialization of a spec_key already present. For DIRECT execution it was deduplicated (build_benchmark_specs dedupes on spec_key), so the identity ran once. It was NOT inert, however: before E3.1 the mutation frontier was seeded from the RAW rows, so a duplicated row entered the frontier twice and changed which mutants survived the target cap (measured on the pre-E3 snapshot: 7 benchmarks, 21 raw-only and 21 canonical-only derived keys, plus fft/08 with the same keys in a different order). Invalid rows had the same effect at larger scale (46 benchmarks, 152/138). E3 removed the duplicate serialization from the cache; E3.1 canonicalizes the frontier so neither can influence mutation again.
retention_equality_semantics: Retained specs are the same parsed JSON objects with the same spec_key and the same input semantics. Six retained lines are not byte-identical to their pre-E3 serialization because non-ASCII characters in the free-text rationale are re-encoded on write; the parsed objects compare equal.
raw_provider_responses_note: The raw provider responses and the full discarded-proposal log of the E3 generation run were not persisted as a frozen artifact. The ACCEPTED artifact is fully version controlled, and the replacement key set, spec_model and generator config fingerprint are recorded here, so the accepted experiment is exactly reusable; the generation process itself is not re-derivable.
